statement: A square sheet of paper is folded in half to make a rectangle, then folded in half again to make a smaller square, four layers thick. One straight cut goes through all the layers, parallel to a side of the small square and halfway between that side and the opposite side. Into how many pieces does the sheet fall?

choices.misconception: I ignored the folds and thought one straight cut always splits a sheet into two pieces.
I thought each of the four layers is cut once, so the sheet gets four cuts in a row and 4 + 1 = 5 pieces.
I thought each of the four layers falls into two pieces, giving 4 × 2 = 8, forgetting that the folds join layers together.
I unfolded the cut in both directions, as if it made two lines across the sheet and two lines down it, a 3 by 3 grid of 9 pieces.

hints: Unfold the paper one fold at a time and draw where the cut goes.
Each unfolding reflects the cut in a fold line. A fold parallel to the cut gives a second cut, but a fold at right angles to the cut only makes the same cut longer.
The cut becomes two straight lines, each running right across the unfolded sheet, parallel to one side and a quarter of the way in from opposite edges.

solutions.reliable: Let the sheet be the square with corners (0, 0) and (4, 4). Fold it along x = 2 and then along y = 2, so the small square has corners (0, 0) and (2, 2), with folds along two of its sides. Suppose the cut is the line x = 1 across the small square. Undo the second fold, along y = 2: the cut is reflected in a line at right angles to it, so it simply continues, and becomes the whole line x = 1 from y = 0 to y = 4. Undo the first fold, along x = 2: the cut is reflected in a parallel line, so a second cut appears along x = 3. Two full cuts across the sheet leave 3 strips. A cut in the other direction, along y = 1, works the same way: unfolding gives full cuts along y = 1 and y = 3, and again 3 pieces. The transferable idea: unfold a cut one fold at a time, reflecting it in each fold line, before counting pieces.
solutions.elegant: Each fold either doubles the cut, if the fold is parallel to it, or just lengthens it, if the fold is at right angles to it. A cut parallel to a side is parallel to exactly one of the two folds, so the open sheet has 2 full cuts and falls into 3 strips.

whyOnTest: Folding and cutting questions test unfolding a cut by reflection, instead of assuming every layer adds more pieces.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
